groups.title: Set membership and deduplication
groups.summary: Choose a set or last-seen map when repeated membership checks dominate the cost.
recognition_signals: The prompt repeatedly asks whether a value has appeared before or belongs to another collection.
The required output depends on uniqueness, duplication, intersection, or the first repeated event.
common_wrong_approaches: Scanning an earlier prefix or another collection for every item creates an avoidable quadratic cost.
Using a set when the contract needs multiplicity or last position discards information required later.

problems.title: First Badge Seen Twice
problems.statement: Employees scan integer badge IDs in chronological order. Return the badge whose second scan occurs first. Return -1 when no badge is scanned more than once.

expected_complexity.space: O(u), where u is the number of distinct badges

problems.title: Final Mention Feed
problems.statement: A feed lists usernames in chronological order. Keep only the final occurrence of each username and preserve the relative chronological order of the entries that remain.

problems.title: Shared Ingredients
problems.statement: Given one or more recipes, each represented by a list of ingredient names, return each distinct ingredient present in every recipe. Order results by first appearance in the first recipe.
constraints: The total number of ingredient entries is at most 100000

expected_complexity.space: O(u), where t is total input size

problems.title: Longest Serial Block
problems.statement: Given unsorted integer serial numbers, return the length of the longest run of consecutive values. Duplicate serial numbers do not extend a run, and sorting is not allowed.

problems.title: Novelty Checkpoints
problems.statement: Given visitor IDs in arrival order, return an array whose value at each index is the number of distinct visitors observed up to and including that arrival.
constraints: Produce one output per input event

problems.title: First Completely New Window
problems.statement: Given an array of event codes and a positive window size, return the starting index of the first fixed-size window in which every value is distinct. Return -1 if no such window exists.
constraints: A window larger than the input has no answer
edge_cases: first valid window at the final position

related_lessons.distinction: This asks for the first valid fixed-size window rather than the longest variable-size unique run.

groups.title: Frequency maps and multisets
groups.summary: Track multiplicity when existence alone cannot prove the result.
recognition_signals: The contract distinguishes one copy from several copies or asks whether resources can be consumed.
The answer depends on how often each value occurs rather than only whether it occurs.
common_wrong_approaches: Replacing counts with a set loses multiplicity and usually passes only all-distinct examples.
Sorting can obscure stable output requirements and costs more than direct counting when keys are hashable.

problems.title: Scrap-Letter Printer
problems.statement: A printer owns reusable character tiles. Determine whether it can print a target message when each tile may be used at most once. Matching is case-sensitive and spaces are ordinary characters.
constraints: Inputs contain UTF-16 code units in the ASCII range

expected_complexity.space: O(a), where a is the observed alphabet

related_lessons.distinction: This checks whether one multiset contains another, not whether two complete inventories are equal.

problems.title: First Unrepeated Alarm
problems.statement: Given alarm codes in chronological order, return the first code that occurs exactly once in the complete sequence. Return null when every code repeats.

problems.title: Missing Shipment Items
problems.statement: Expected and actual shipments are arrays of item IDs. Return the missing items in expected-shipment order, preserving multiplicity. Extra actual items do not appear in the result.

related_lessons.distinction: This computes an ordered multiset difference instead of returning whole-inventory equality.

problems.title: Unique Popularity Counts
problems.statement: Return true when every distinct integer in an array occurs a different number of times. Empty and single-distinct-value arrays satisfy the condition.

problems.title: Shortest Representative Log
problems.primary_concept: frequency with first and last positions
problems.statement: The degree of an array is its greatest value frequency. Return the inclusive boundaries of the shortest contiguous subarray having the same degree as the complete array. Break equal lengths by earlier start.
constraints: Return a pair of inclusive indices

problems.title: Equal-Frequency Removal
problems.statement: Determine whether deleting exactly one array element can make every remaining distinct value occur the same positive number of times. The empty remainder is valid.
constraints: Exactly one element must be deleted

groups.title: Complement lookup and pair counting
groups.summary: Compute the value or remainder needed to complete a relation, then count earlier matches.
recognition_signals: For each current value, the relationship determines one or a small number of needed partner values.
The prompt asks for pairs or tuples satisfying a fixed sum, difference, XOR, product, or remainder relation.
common_wrong_approaches: Enumerating every pair ignores that a partner can be derived directly from the current value.
Inserting the current item before counting partners can accidentally pair an index with itself.

problems.title: Firmware Version Gap
problems.statement: Given integer version numbers and a nonnegative gap d, count unordered index pairs (i, j), i < j, for which the absolute value difference is exactly d.
constraints: The answer fits in a safe integer

related_lessons.distinction: This counts every absolute-difference index pair and must treat a zero gap separately.

problems.title: Closest-in-Time Target Pair
problems.primary_concept: complement lookup with nearest prior index
problems.statement: Among all distinct event pairs whose numeric values sum to target, return the pair of indices with minimum distance. Break ties by smaller second index, then smaller first index. Return null if none exists.
constraints: Values and target are safe integers

related_lessons.distinction: The workshop lesson accepts any valid pair; this variant optimizes index distance with explicit ties.

problems.title: XOR Access Keys
problems.statement: Given nonnegative integer access keys and a target bitmask, count unordered index pairs whose bitwise XOR equals the target bitmask.
constraints: The answer fits in a safe integer

related_lessons.distinction: The complement is derived with XOR and every index pair is counted rather than one pair returned.

problems.title: Full-Cycle Song Pairs
problems.statement: Given song durations and a positive cycle length m, count unordered index pairs whose combined duration is divisible by m. Durations may be negative offsets.
constraints: The answer fits in a safe integer
edge_cases: m/2 remainder when m is even

problems.title: Four-Ledger Reconciliation
problems.statement: Given four equally sized integer ledgers A, B, C, and D, count index tuples (i, j, k, l) for which A[i] + B[j] + C[k] + D[l] equals zero.
constraints: The answer fits in a safe integer

related_lessons.distinction: This extends complement lookup to four arrays with pair-sum multiplicities and meet-in-the-middle.

problems.title: Product Partner
problems.statement: Determine whether two distinct indices contain integers whose product equals target. Avoid multiplication overflow by deriving a partner only when division is exact; handle zero explicitly.
constraints: Values and target are safe integers
Intermediate multiplication may exceed the safe-integer range
edge_cases: target not divisible by current value

related_lessons.distinction: The relation is multiplication, so zero, sign, exact division, and overflow change complement derivation.

groups.title: Canonical representation and grouping
groups.summary: Normalize equivalent objects to one stable key before deduplicating or grouping them.
recognition_signals: Objects may look different syntactically but the contract defines transformations that preserve equivalence.
The task asks to group or deduplicate values under rotation, translation, scaling, or normalization rules.
common_wrong_approaches: Comparing every pair of objects repeats expensive equivalence work and tends toward quadratic time.
An incomplete sign, order, or zero convention creates multiple keys for the same logical value.

problems.title: Anagram Filing System
problems.statement: Group lowercase words that contain the same letters with the same multiplicities. Preserve word order inside each group and order groups by the first word assigned to them.
constraints: Words contain only lowercase English letters
Total character count is at most 100000

expected_complexity.space: O(c), where c is total characters

problems.title: Shift-Equivalent Labels
problems.statement: Group nonempty lowercase labels when every character of one can be shifted by the same cyclic alphabet offset to form the other. Preserve input order within and across groups.
constraints: Each label contains lowercase English letters
Total character count is at most 100000

problems.title: Direction Families
problems.statement: Group nonzero integer vectors that point along the same directed ray. Vectors with opposite signs belong to different groups. Preserve the first-seen order of groups and vectors.
constraints: Each component is a safe integer
The zero vector is not allowed

problems.title: Translated Island Shapes
problems.statement: A binary grid contains 4-directionally connected islands. Return the number of distinct island shapes when translation is allowed but rotation and reflection are not.

related_lessons.distinction: This traverses components and additionally canonicalizes each component's geometry under translation.

problems.title: Necklace Families
problems.statement: Group equal-length strings when one is a cyclic rotation of the other. Reversal is not allowed. Preserve input order inside groups and first-seen group order.
constraints: Total character count is at most 200000
Strings may contain arbitrary ASCII characters

expected_complexity.time: O(c) with a linear minimum-rotation algorithm

problems.title: Rational Number Deduplication
problems.statement: Given integer numerator-denominator pairs, return the number of distinct numeric values. Reduce by greatest common divisor, keep denominators positive, and represent every zero identically.
constraints: Numerators and denominators are safe integers

groups.title: Prefix sums and prefix-state hashing
groups.summary: Describe a range by subtracting or comparing cumulative state at two boundaries.
recognition_signals: The prompt asks about many contiguous ranges, or negative values prevent a monotonic sliding window.
A valid range can be recognized by a relationship between state before the range and state after it.
common_wrong_approaches: Recomputing each range aggregate repeats work and often produces quadratic or query-times-length cost.
Forgetting the empty prefix loses ranges that begin at index zero and causes off-by-one errors.

problems.title: Historical Balance Queries
problems.statement: Given daily account changes and many inclusive [left, right] queries, return the total change for each query. Preprocess once rather than scanning each queried range.
constraints: Every query indexes a valid nonempty range

problems.title: Target-Sum Periods
problems.statement: Count contiguous nonempty periods whose values sum exactly to k. Values may be positive, negative, or zero, so window sums are not monotonic.
constraints: Values and k are safe integers
The answer fits in a safe integer

problems.title: Longest Balanced Signal
problems.statement: Given a binary signal, return the length of the longest contiguous segment containing an equal number of zeros and ones.

problems.title: Divisible Expense Periods
problems.statement: Count contiguous nonempty expense periods whose total is divisible by positive integer m. Expense adjustments may be negative; normalize remainders into 0 through m - 1.
constraints: The answer fits in a safe integer

problems.title: Equal Red, Green, and Blue Segment
problems.statement: A signal contains only R, G, and B. Return the inclusive boundaries of the longest contiguous segment with equal counts of all three symbols. Break ties by earliest start; return null if none exists.
constraints: The alphabet is exactly R, G, and B
A valid segment must be nonempty

problems.title: Odd-Parity Character Window
problems.statement: Given a string over letters a through j, return the length of the longest substring in which at most one distinct character has an odd frequency.
constraints: Text contains only letters a through j

examples.explanation: The complete string has only b with odd frequency.

groups.title: Difference arrays and event sweeps
groups.summary: Apply range effects at boundaries, then reconstruct state in sorted order.
recognition_signals: Many operations affect complete ranges while only their start and end boundaries change the active state.
Coordinates may be sparse or huge, but the answer changes only at a limited set of event positions.
common_wrong_approaches: Updating every point in every interval makes runtime depend on total covered length rather than event count.
Failing to define inclusive versus half-open endpoints produces incorrect ordering for simultaneous events.

problems.title: Batch Temperature Adjustments
problems.statement: Start with an integer array of n zeros. Each operation [left, right, delta] adds delta to every inclusive index in the range. Return the final array after all operations.
constraints: Every operation is within 0 through n - 1

problems.title: Shuttle Capacity Audit
problems.statement: Each trip [passengers, pickup, dropoff] boards passengers at pickup and removes them before boarding at dropoff. Return whether shuttle occupancy ever exceeds capacity.
constraints: Passengers and capacity are nonnegative safe integers
edge_cases: dropoff and pickup at same stop

related_lessons.distinction: Events carry passenger weights and dropoffs occur before pickups, rather than counting uniform rooms.

problems.title: Streetlight Brightness
problems.statement: Each streetlight illuminates every integer position in an inclusive interval [left, right]. Return the number of integer positions covered by at least k lights.

problems.title: Peak Session Intervals
problems.statement: Sessions use half-open intervals [login, logout). Return the maximum concurrent session count and every maximal half-open interval over which that maximum is maintained. Ignore zero-length intervals.
constraints: Each login time is at most its logout time
edge_cases: logout and login at same time

related_lessons.distinction: This returns all maximal peak intervals with explicit half-open semantics, not only a room count.

problems.title: Earliest Overloaded Time
problems.statement: Workloads are half-open intervals [start, end) with positive amounts. Return the earliest coordinate at which active workload strictly exceeds the system limit, or null if it never does.
constraints: Use bigint coordinates and workload totals

related_lessons.distinction: This uses weighted sparse events, strict overload detection, and coordinates requiring bigint arithmetic.

problems.title: Covered-Length Report
problems.statement: Given half-open real-coordinate intervals [start, end), return the total length covered by at least one interval. Zero-length intervals contribute nothing.
constraints: Each start is at most its end

expected_complexity.space: O(n) because the input is preserved

related_lessons.distinction: This computes continuous union length under half-open semantics rather than returning merged intervals.

groups.title: Values used as indices and permutation cycles
groups.summary: Exploit a constrained value range as implicit storage or as a pointer graph.
recognition_signals: Array values are restricted to an index-sized range such as zero through n or one through n.
The contract requires linear time with constant auxiliary space or describes a permutation and its cycles.
common_wrong_approaches: Using a general set ignores information encoded by the constrained value range and violates space limits.
Swapping without checking whether a value is already correctly placed can create an infinite duplicate loop.

problems.title: Missing Shelf Labels
problems.statement: An array of length n contains integers from 1 through n with repetition allowed. Return all values in that range that do not appear, using constant auxiliary space besides the result.
constraints: Every value is between 1 and n

related_lessons.distinction: Both permit mutation, but this encodes presence through value-index correspondence rather than two pointers.

problems.title: Corrupted Permutation
problems.statement: An intended permutation of 1 through n contains one duplicated value and one missing value. Return an object containing both, using constant auxiliary space.
constraints: Every value is between 1 and n

problems.title: First Missing Positive Identifier
problems.statement: Given an unsorted integer array containing negatives, zeros, and positives, return the smallest positive integer that does not appear. Use linear time and constant auxiliary space.

problems.title: Restore Seat Assignments
problems.statement: Array seatOfStudent is a permutation where index is a student and value is the seat currently occupied. Return the minimum swaps of any two students needed so every student i occupies seat i.
constraints: Values form a permutation of 0 through n - 1

problems.title: Read-Only Duplicate Search
problems.statement: An array of length n + 1 contains values from 1 through n and exactly one distinct value is duplicated one or more times. Return that value without modifying the array and with constant auxiliary space.
constraints: Every value is between 1 and n
Run in O(n) time and do not mutate input

related_lessons.distinction: This models array values as pointers and must locate the cycle entry, not merely detect a linked-list cycle.

problems.title: Broken Circular Routing Table
problems.primary_concept: cycle metrics in a functional graph
problems.statement: Each routing-table entry stores the index of the next entry. Starting from entry 0, return whether a cycle exists, its first entry, its length, and the number of entries before it. A route that exits with -1 is acyclic.
constraints: Each value is -1 or a valid index
Do not mutate the routing table

expected_complexity.time: O(r), where r is reachable entries

related_lessons.distinction: This returns entry, cycle length, and tail length for an index graph and also supports an acyclic sentinel.
